Bases: BaseSettings

Application settings and configuration.

Uses Pydantic BaseSettings to load configuration from environment variables and .env files. Provides centralized access to all application settings including paths, credentials, logging levels, and operational parameters.

Settings Categories

Application Settings:

APP_NAME, ENVIRONMENT, LOG_LEVEL, VERSION, CURRENCY

Platform Settings:

OS_TYPE, MULTIPROCESSING_CONTEXT, MIN_PROCESS_COUNT, MIN_WORKER_COUNT

APP_NAME: str

Application name - Default is “SQRL”

Type:

str

ENVIRONMENT: str

Application environment - Default is “development”

Type:

str

LOG_LEVEL: str

Logging level - Default is “INFO”

Type:

str

Application version - Read from pyproject.toml

Type:

str

OS_TYPE: str

Operating system type - Automatically detected using platform.system()

Type:

str

MULTIPROCESSING_CONTEXT: str

Multiprocessing context - “spawn” for Windows, “fork” for Unix-based systems

Type:

str

MIN_PROCESS_COUNT: int

Minimum number of processes - Default is 2

Type:

int

MIN_WORKER_COUNT: int

Minimum number of workers - Default is 4

Type:

int

class squirrel.core.config.Colors[source]

Bases: object

ANSI color codes for terminal output formatting.

Provides constants for colorizing terminal output with standard ANSI escape codes. Useful for making console logs and output more readable and visually distinct.

Color Constants

HEADER - Purple color for headers OKBLUE - Blue color for informational messages OKCYAN - Cyan color for progress indicators OKGREEN - Green color for success messages WARNING - Yellow color for warnings FAIL - Red color for error messages BOLD - Bold text formatting UNDERLINE - Underlined text formatting RED - Bright red color ENDC - End color formatting

Example usage:

print(f"{Colors.OKGREEN}Success!{Colors.ENDC}")
print(f"{Colors.WARNING}Warning message{Colors.ENDC}")
HEADER = '\x1b[95m'

ANSI escape code for purple color (headers)

str
